t: Islam began with the revelations that Muslims believe the prophet Muhammad received from God through the angel Gabriel in Mecca from 610, gathered in the Quran: there is no god but God, and Muhammad is his messenger.
Within a century of Muhammad’s death in 632 the caliphs ruled from Spain to Central Asia; traders, scholars and Sufis later carried Islam across Africa, India and Southeast Asia.
Divided since the first century into Sunni and Shia traditions, it shaped law, learning, art and the Arabic language across a vast civilisation and is today the faith of about two billion people.
dyk: The Islamic calendar counts years from Muhammad’s migration from Mecca to Medina in 622; because it is a lunar calendar, its months move through the seasons, and the fast of Ramadan comes about eleven days earlier each year.
ev: Muhammad receives his first revelation in the cave of Hira near Mecca, according to Islamic tradition
The Hijra: Muhammad and his followers migrate from Mecca to Medina, the start of the Islamic calendar
Muhammad dies in Medina; Abu Bakr becomes the first caliph
The caliph Uthman has the text of the Quran gathered and copies sent to the main cities
Husayn, Muhammad’s grandson, is killed at Karbala, an event central to Shia Islam
The Dome of the Rock is completed in Jerusalem
Muslim armies cross from North Africa into Spain
The Republic of Turkey abolishes the Ottoman caliphate

f.origin: Mecca and Medina, in western Arabia, from 610
f.founder: The prophet Muhammad (c. 570–632), the last of the prophets in Islamic belief
f.scriptures: The Quran; the hadith, reports of the words and deeds of Muhammad
f.followers: About 2 billion (2020), the second-largest religion; the largest Muslim country is Indonesia
